summary: Inline round-4 review: most round-3 fixes are implemented, but account-stop handling remains incomplete. Offline reproductions also confirmed credential exposure when overwriting an insecure existing cookie file and a race that bypasses pending-publish protection. Type-checking passed; the Bun suite and live Instagram calls were not run.

prior_blockers.title: Windows isolation accepts a different account with the same username
prior_blockers.evidence: secure.ts now compares qualified account names exactly and removes other principals before checking the ACL again (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/secure.ts:46, secure.ts:71, secure.ts:75). The separate existing-file exposure described below remains.

prior_blockers.title: Corrupt or unreadable pending state silently permits another publish
prior_blockers.evidence: Non-ENOENT directory errors now throw; unreadable or invalid JSON records become unresolved placeholders (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/pending.ts:55, pending.ts:63, pending.ts:66). executePlan blocks on those records (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:426). Offline mocks confirmed both cases block.

prior_blockers.title: Ambiguous mutation responses can trigger a second write automatically
prior_blockers.evidence: Bare HTTP 202 no longer implies transcode_pending (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/client.ts:143). Mutation fallback requires HTTP 404 (client.ts:293), and comment/delete callers enable that restriction (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:490, publish.ts:513). Offline mocks confirmed one configure for ambiguous 202/network/502 responses and one comment POST without a returned ID. The previously identified 11-versus-10 attempt discrepancy remains (publish.ts:374, publish.ts:384).

prior_blockers.title: Unproven mutations remain outside the experimental gate
prior_blockers.evidence: requireGate now requires experimental opt-in for every status other than verified-live (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/main.ts:124). Publishing and management commands invoke it before creating a client (main.ts:138, main.ts:351); no contract is currently verified-live (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:23).

prior_blockers.title: Some checkpoint responses do not stop subsequent account requests
prior_blockers.evidence: GraphQL messages without data now classify checkpoint/login/feedback signals, and JSON-mode HTML responses recognize challenge pages (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/graphql.ts:133; instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/client.ts:256). Partial GraphQL data still suppresses error handling (graphql.ts:131), and expectJson:false returns HTML before checking account signals (client.ts:244). Both remaining bypasses reproduced offline.

prior_blockers.title: The live-test preload discards the session required by the documented test command
prior_blockers.evidence: The preload now preserves session sources and pacing when INSTAGRAM_LIVE=1 (instagram-ai-plugin/test/unit/setup.ts:8). Both documented live commands set that flag, and writes additionally require INSTAGRAM_LIVE_WRITE=1 (instagram-ai-plugin/test/live.test.ts:4, live.test.ts:26). This was verified from source, without live execution.

strengths: Authenticated requests enforce HTTPS, restrict destinations to Instagram hosts, and disable redirects; CDN discovery fetches supply no cookies (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/client.ts:199, client.ts:223; instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/constants.ts:22; instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/graphql.ts:85).

Dry-run branches return before client creation, and previews use redacted authentication headers. Targeted Node-based mocked CLI checks observed zero fetches in tested dry runs and experimental-gate refusals (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/main.ts:133, main.ts:347; instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:313).

Ordinary ambiguous configure outcomes preserve pending state without replay; caption matching never automatically resolves a publish (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:408, publish.ts:438, publish.ts:454).

Automatic configure retries require an explicit transcode-pending error and video content; photo transcode errors were not retried in offline checks (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/publish.ts:383).

Research limits are enforced, default authenticated request pacing is 1.5 seconds, and the CLI exposes no like, follow or DM commands (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/main.ts:300, main.ts:306; instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/constants.ts:54).
TypeScript validation passed with the supplied test/tsconfig.json and --noEmit.

blocking_findings.title: Partial GraphQL responses and HTML discovery pages still bypass account-stop handling
blocking_findings.why: The operation can continue making authenticated requests after receiving an explicit checkpoint signal, contradicting the safety contract.
blocking_findings.evidence: GraphQL examines errors only when data is absent. A mocked response containing timeline data plus challenge_required caused getPosts to issue a second GraphQL pagination request. Separately, expectJson:false returned a challenge HTML page unchanged; GraphQL initialization then failed as an ordinary discovery error, and getPosts sent another authenticated profile request.

blocking_findings.title: Existing Windows cookie files receive credentials before their own permissions are secured
blocking_findings.why: Restricting the parent directory does not remove explicit grants on an existing child file. Overwriting that file can expose newly imported or rotated credentials before its ACL is repaired or the file is deleted.
blocking_findings.evidence: writeCookieMapToDisk secures the directory, writes cookie bytes, and only then calls ensurePrivateFile. The directory icacls operation targets the directory itself. An offline ACL mock retaining another reader on the existing cookie file produced WRITE_COOKIE_BYTES before restrict-file, followed by InsecureStorageError and deletion. The claim that nothing is saved when isolation fails therefore does not hold for this case.

blocking_findings.title: Overlapping publishes bypass the pending ledger's duplicate protection
blocking_findings.why: Two invocations can both pass the empty-ledger check before either records its configure operation. The second can subsequently publish the same content even after the first becomes unresolved.
blocking_findings.evidence: The ledger is checked once before uploads, while the pending record is created only after uploads. There is no exclusive reservation or recheck before configure. An in-memory reproduction started two overlapping publishes, made the first configure fail ambiguously, verified its unresolved record, and then allowed the second configure to succeed without ignorePending or human resolution.

non_blocking_findings.title: The previously reported transcode attempt-count discrepancy remains
non_blocking_findings.why: The implementation exceeds the plan's stated request budget by one configure POST. This is bounded and restricted to explicit video-processing responses, so it is not the earlier ambiguous-response replay defect.
non_blocking_findings.evidence: Ten backoff entries permit ten retries after the initial request. An offline mock that always returned transcode_pending counted 11 configure attempts; PLAN.md specifies 10 attempts.

open_questions: No live Instagram calls were made. Actual mutation payloads, response semantics, and server-side retry/idempotency behavior remain unverified; keeping every write experimental is appropriate.

The earlier GraphQL compatibility concern remains unproven: response-root selection is heuristic, and the live read test accepts an empty array without requiring GraphQL or exercising pagination (instagram-ai-plugin/skills/instagram/scripts/graphql.ts:185; instagram-ai-plugin/test/live.test.ts:36). Which sanitized operation and pagination fixtures establish those contracts?

The full Bun suite was not executed: Bun was unavailable on PATH and its fixtures require filesystem writes. Runtime reproductions used Node with TypeScript transformation and mocked filesystem/network operations; actual Windows ACL behavior was not exercised.
